{{Current events|year=2026|month=06|day=23|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign]]
*****The [[International Maritime Organization]] announces an evacuation plan for around 500 to 600 ships with 11,000 seafarers stranded in the [[Persian Gulf]] to sail through the [[Strait of Hormuz]] after [[Iran]] and the [[United States]] have reached a [[2026 Iran war ceasefire|ceasefire]] [[Islamabad Memorandum|deal]] to end the [[war]]. The evacuation will be coordinated with Iran and [[Oman]]. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/un-shipping-agency-announces-evacuation-11000-seafarers-stranded-gulf (''Middle East Eye)''] [https://maritime-executive.com/article/imo-and-oman-launch-phased-evacuation-for-transits-in-strait-of-hormuz (The Maritime Executive)] 
****The [[Bangladesh Shipping Corporation]] reports that the [[Bangladesh]]-flagged [[Deadweight tonnage|DWT]] [[bulk carrier]] vessel MV ''Banglar Joyjatra'' has cleared through the Strait of Hormuz at 3:00am [[Bangladesh Standard Time|BST]] after it was stranded in the region for 4.5 months. [https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/banglar-joyjatra-clears-strait-hormuz-after-four-and-half-month-ordeal-1469926 (''The Business Standard'')] [https://www.newagebd.net/post/foreign-affairs/303704/bangladeshi-ship-banglar-joyjatra-crosses-strait-of-hormuz (''New Age BD'')]
****[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Marco Rubio]] says that the U.S. will not accept Iranian tolls or fees on vessels transiting through the Strait of Hormuz. [https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/921719/us-secretary-of-state-rejects-iranian-tolls-on-strait-of-hormuz (Kurdistan24)] 
***[[2026 United States F-15E rescue operation in Iran]]
****Two sources tell [[CNN]] that a pilot on a [[United States Armed Forces]] [[McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle|F-15E Strike Eagle]], which was downed over [[Iran]] during the beginning of April, reported a "[[jellyfish]]-like" formation from [[Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Iranian military|Iranian drones]] before the jet was shot down. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/us-israel-iran-war/downed-us-f-15-pilot-describes-multiple-iranian-drones-in-jellyfish-formation-report/3975773 (AA)] [https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/23/politics/iran-drones-f-15-pilot-intelligence (CNN)]
**[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
***[[Gaza war]]
****The [[Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory]] finds that [[Israel]] has deliberately targeted [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] children, resulting in [[Gaza genocide|genocide]], crimes against humanity, [[War crimes in the Gaza war|war crimes in Gaza]], and war crimes in the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-targeted-gaza-children-resulting-genocide-un-inquiry-says-2026-06-23/ (Reuters)]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[Israel]]i soldiers open fire near an [[excavator]] in [[Nabatieh]], [[Lebanon]], killing two civilians and wounding two more. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/23/israeli-fire-kills-two-in-lebanon-as-hezbollah-slams-truce-violation (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[2026 Blue Nile campaign]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces|Sudanese army]] launches an [[Offensive (military)|offensive]] in the [[Geissan District]] of [[Sudan]]'s [[Blue Nile State]], capturing a key rebel stronghold near [[Ethiopia–Sudan border|the border]] with [[Ethiopia]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/315409 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**[[War crimes during the Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|War crimes during the Sudanese civil war]]
***The [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights|U.N. Human Rights Office]] reports that [[sexual violence]] has been more widespread across Sudan since the [[civil war]] broke out three years ago in April. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crel587qz8ro (BBC News)] [https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/u-n-report-documents-widespread-sexual-violence-in-sudan-conflict (Radio Tamazuj)]
*[[Communal conflicts in Nigeria]]
**[[Nigeria]]n [[Nigeria Police Force|police]] report that at least 20 people were killed in an attack on a community in [[Bokkos]], [[Plateau State]], over the weekend. Police and other [[Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps|security agencies]] engaged the assailants in a [[shootout]] before they withdrew from the area. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/attack-kills-20-nigerias-central-plateau-attack-2026-06-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 European heatwaves]]
**[[Minister of Sports (France)|French sports minister]] [[Marina Ferrari]] reports that at least 40 people have drowned in [[France]] while swimming in unsupervised areas over the weekend during a [[heat wave]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/23/about-20-drown-in-france-trying-to-escape-heatwave-sweeping-much-of-europe (AFP and Reuters via Al Jazeera)]

'''International relations'''
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]], [[North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Prisoners of war in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Prisoners of war in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[South Korea]] announces that it will accept any [[North Korea]]n [[prisoners of war]] captured by [[Ukraine]] while [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|fighting]] for [[Russia]] if they choose resettlement in South Korea. South Korea also opposes any repatriation of such prisoners against their wishes. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-korea-accept-all-north-korean-pows-ukraine-if-they-desire-ministry-says-2026-06-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Libyan crisis]]
**The [[Government of National Stability]], which controls eastern [[Libya]], prohibits the entry of citizens of [[Eritrea]], [[Ethiopia]], [[Somalia]], and [[Sudan]] through all land, sea and air ports, citing a reorganization of procedures governing the entry of foreign nationals. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/libyas-eastern-government-bans-entry-nationals-four-african-countries-2026-06-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Reactions to the 2026 Iran war]]
**The [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] votes 50–48 in favor of a [[War Powers Resolution|resolution]] to require the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] to halt [[United States Armed Forces|military]] action against Iran, joining the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] in doing so. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jun/23/trump-iran-war-powers-resolution (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/senate-rebukes-trump-approving-house-passed-iran-war-powers-resolution-rcna351445 (NBC News)] [https://www.npr.org/2026/06/23/nx-s1-5868599/senate-iran-war-powers-resolution (NPR)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 FIFA World Cup]]
**[[Portugal at the FIFA World Cup]]
***In [[association football]], [[Portugal national football team|Portuguese]] [[Forward (association football)|forward]] and captain [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] becomes the first player to score in six different [[FIFA World Cup]]s and [[Portugal national football team records and statistics|Portugal's all-time top goalscorer]] at the tournament after scoring a [[Brace (association football)|brace]] in the team's 5–0 win over [[Uzbekistan national football team|Uzbekistan]] in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group K|group stage]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260623-portugal-s-ronaldo-first-man-to-score-at-six-world-cups (AFP via RFI)]
